case_name: Jai Kumar v State Of Haryana
respondent:
State Of Haryana
Supreme Court of India

21 July 2009
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO. 1285 OF 2009(Arising out of SLP (Crl.) No.8930 of 2008)
The Judgment was delivered by : S. B. Sinha, J.
Leave granted.
1.  The appellant is before us claiming parity with his co-accused Subhash 2007 Indlaw SC 854 for obtaining the benefit of a judgment of this Court in Subhash v. State of Haryana since reported in [(2007) 12 SCC 63 2007 Indlaw SC 854].
2.  At the outset, we would like to place on record that this appeal is barred by 896 days. Ordinarily, we would not have condoned the delay but we had issued notice both on SLP as also on the application for condonation of delay only on the premise that the appellant had raised a contention before this Court that he and his co-accused Subhash 2007 Indlaw SC 854 are similarly situated.
3.  Appellant was charged for commission of offences punishable under Sections 392, 397 and 302/34 of the Indian Penal Code. The occurrence took place on 9.10.1991. A Fir

statutes.act: Read With Section 34 Of The Indian Penal Code

facts: One Mane Ram (PW8) who alleged that he along with the deceased Raghbir Singh had gone to village Kaillana in a tractor to bring 'barma' (an instrument for drawing water) from one Nandlal.
Son of Basu Sardar took away the nip of liquor from the deceased and consumed it.
All of them again consumed some illicit liquor.
For some reasons or the other, an altercation took place between son of Basu Sardar, Subhash 2007 Indlaw SC 854 and Jai Kumar.
Joginder Singh drove the tractor towards village Bajana along the bank of a canal.
The deceased tried to save himself by catching hold of the grass grown on the bank of the canal.
He was kicked on the face and again thrown in the canal.
court_reasoning: The evidence available on record does not suggest that there has been any intention of causing the death of Raghbir (the deceased).
The case falls under Part II of Section 304 IPC.
The appellant committed the offence of culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
There is no merit in the appeal.
holding: The sentence of rigorous imprisonment for a period of 7 years for each of the offence under Section 392 read with Section 397 IPC is accordingly upheld.
The appellant is accordingly convicted under Part II of Section 304 IPC and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 7 years.
